issue.title: sase-listen has never published to PyPI: release-please cannot open release PRs and the hand-opened 0.1.0 PR was never tagged
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1e3.1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #1), sase-1e3.11 (#3) and sase-1e3.12 (#3); triaged by the sase-1e3 land agent on 2026-10-01.

sase-org/sase-listen has no release on PyPI (https://pypi.org/pypi/sase-listen/json is 404), no git tags and no GitHub releases, although the 0.1.0 release PR (#1) was merged at ef84b3b.

Root cause (two parts):
1. release-please cannot open release PRs. The repo has no `SASE_RELEASE_TOKEN` secret (sibling repos such as sase-telegram have a repo-level one), and org policy keeps `can_approve_pull_request_reviews=false`, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create PRs. Every master push's Publish run fails with "GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests" (runs 36936340589, 36939459705).
2. Release PR #1 was opened by hand from the bot branch, so it never got the `autorelease: pending` label. After the merge, release-please logged "No latest release pull request found" and created no tag or release, so `release_created` stayed false and build/install-smoke/publish never ran. It has since pushed a `chore(master): release 0.1.1` commit (5326fea) to the bot branch, but cannot open that PR either.

Remedy:
- (User) Add a `SASE_RELEASE_TOKEN` repo secret to sase-org/sase-listen (the same kind of PAT the sibling repos use), or allow Actions to create PRs at the org level. Agents cannot read or copy secret values.
- Give release-please a v0.1.0 baseline. Either label merged PR #1 `autorelease: pending` before the next Publish run, so release-please tags v0.1.0 at ef84b3b and publishes, or create the v0.1.0 tag and release at ef84b3b by hand and publish with the `workflow_dispatch` `publish_existing=true` escape hatch.
- Merge the next release PR (it should carry the CLI rebuild from the sase-1e3 landing tale) through a `/sase_gate`. Then confirm the Publish run succeeded and that PyPI lists the version.
- On apollo, replace the git-source install with `uv tool install --force sase-listen` from PyPI.
